display.purpose: Hero headline only; two lines maximum, tight tracking.

accent.purpose: Italic emphasis words inside headings; never a whole heading.

headline.purpose: Section headings across all six bands.

body.purpose: Paragraphs and supporting copy; measure capped at 460–560px.

label.purpose: Buttons, partner strip label, CTA contact label, copyright.

shadows.name: mobile-nav
shadows.purpose: Separates the open mobile menu from the hero photograph. The only resting shadow in the system.

motion.name: state-default
motion.purpose: Hover and focus transitions on links, buttons, and borders.

motion.name: lift
motion.purpose: Single button hover lift; no other choreography.

narrative.overview: The landing page should feel like walking into a well-run estate office: quiet, ordered, and confident. The paper ground, square edges, and hairline rules do the work that decoration would otherwise do. Photography supplies the warmth; typography supplies the authority. The system is deliberately sparse. There are six sections, each with one job: hero, partners, confidence, built-for, CTA, footer. Sections change tone through full-bleed ground shifts — paper, deep pine, warm orange — rather than through cards, shadows, or ornament. The orange is a committed brand signal, not a sprinkle: it carries the primary action and one drenched band. Emphasis inside headlines is always the same move: Manrope for the claim, DM Serif Display italic for the human half of the sentence.
keyCharacteristics: Paper-first neutral ground with three full-bleed tonal bands.
Manrope display paired with DM Serif Display italic accents.
Square edges, 1px hairline rules, zero resting shadows.
Photographic hero; no illustration, no icon-card grid.
Small, wide-tracked uppercase labels for wayfinding.

rules.name: The One Band Rule
rules.body: Orange is allowed one full-bleed section per page. Everywhere else it appears only as a button, a mark, or a 28px rule.

rules.name: The No White Body Rule
rules.body: Small text on Commit Orange uses Ink on Commit, not white. White on orange fails 4.5:1 below large-text sizes.

rules.name: The Split Headline Rule
rules.body: Every section heading ends in DM Serif Display italic. Never set a full heading in the serif, and never set the accent word in the same sans as the claim.

rules.name: The Two-Line Rule
rules.body: Display headlines break at a meaningful clause boundary, never mid-phrase. At 1440px, "Better managed." and "Better for life." each hold one line.

rules.name: The No Card Rule
rules.body: Content is separated by hairlines and ground shifts, never by elevated boxes.

dos: Do keep one full-bleed orange band per page and use orange elsewhere only as action, mark, or rule.
Do pair Manrope claims with DM Serif Display italic accent words in every heading.
Do separate content with 1px rules and tonal ground shifts.
Do put Ink or Ink on Commit text on orange surfaces.
Do preserve both auth paths: operator /login and resident /resident/login, plus /onboard.
donts: Don't use white body text on Commit Orange.
Don't introduce cards, shadows, rounded corners, or glass panels.
Don't add eyebrow kickers, section numbers, or a metric strip above headlines.
Don't set an entire heading in the serif accent face.
Don't replace the square button language with pills.
Don't invent partner logos or claims; the partner strip lists categories, not companies.
